title: The vow of refuge
hookLine: a spear meant for Vibhishana, a brother who steps in front of it, and a chariot sent from heaven
carry: sharanagati: whoever comes for refuge is safe

cards: Ravana has no one left to send. His brother Kumbhakarna is dead. His son Indrajit is dead.
Most of his champions are gone. So he puts on his armor, mounts his great chariot, and rides out through the gates himself, with whatever army remains. The monkeys scatter before him.
And in the enemy line he sees the brother who left him, Vibhishana. Ravana picks up a great spear, made to kill, and aims it at him.

teach.b: Lakshmana sees it, and doesn't hesitate. He fires at Ravana again and again, drawing his attention away from Vibhishana.
Remember the shore, when Vibhishana came across the sea asking for refuge and the monkeys wanted him killed as a spy.

teach.h: SHARANAGATI: WHOEVER COMES FOR REFUGE IS SAFE.
teach.b: Rama said: whoever comes to me even once, saying I am yours, I give safety from every being. That is my vow.
Hindus call this sharanagati, taking refuge, and in some traditions, like the Sri Vaishnavas of South India, that verse is treasured as God's own promise to anyone who surrenders.
Now Lakshmana keeps the vow with his body. Ravana turns the spear on him: you saved him, so take this instead.
It strikes Lakshmana in the chest, and he falls. Rama pulls it out, breaks it, and weeps beside his brother. What would I do with victory without Lakshmana?
Sushena, the monkey physician, says he isn't dead; his face hasn't changed. Once more Hanuman brings herbs from a mountain. Sushena holds one to Lakshmana's nose, and he breathes it in and gets up.

Then Indra sends his own chariot down to Rama, who has fought this whole war on foot, with his charioteer, Matali, at the reins. Rama walks around it with respect and climbs aboard. Ravana in his chariot, Rama in Indra's.

how: Ramlila performances across North India build toward Ravana's final battle over many nights. Many follow Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas, where the wounding of Lakshmana that audiences know best comes earlier, from Meghnad (Indrajit), and Sushena and Hanuman's mountain save him there.

o: Ravana's charioteer, who drives him out through the gates
a monkey general who guards Rama's camp at night
Indra's charioteer, who brings Rama a chariot from the sky

games.q: the vow of refuge — tap the pairs.
p: draws the spear away from Vibhishana
whoever says "I am yours" is safe

s: Ravana's spear was first aimed at Lakshmana
it was aimed at Vibhishana; Lakshmana drew it onto himself.
Rama promised refuge only to his own allies
his vow covers anyone who comes even once saying "I am yours", even the enemy's brother.
Rama fought most of the war on foot
until Indra sent his chariot with Matali.

games.q: you're Lakshmana. Ravana is about to hurl a spear at Vibhishana, who came to Rama for refuge. what do you do?
games.why: he shoots at Ravana until Ravana turns the spear on him, and he falls in Vibhishana's place, keeping Rama's vow of refuge with his own body.

practice: Many Hindus say a short line of refuge, often at night, like Shri Rama sharanam mama: Rama, you are my refuge. If you pray, say it slowly a few times, and hand over one thing you can't carry tonight.
If you don't, think of someone who has made you safe, and picture one way you could be that shelter for someone else this week.

wordCard.voice: Matali. Indra's charioteer, who brings down Indra's chariot so Rama can meet Ravana as an equal, after a spear aimed at Vibhishana and Sushena's healing herb brought Lakshmana back.

orig.note: Sanskrit śaraṇāgati: coming for refuge, from śaraṇa, shelter, and āgati, arrival; the surrender Rama vows to protect.

carryVoice: Your line: sharanagati, whoever comes for refuge is safe. A tired man and a hymn come next. That's day six hundred fifty-four.
